text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The University of Zambia has suspended five administrative managers, bringing to seven the number of senior officials suspended at the institution this year.
- A Ugandan national has been arrested for carrying 20 passports in his name.
- Mines Minister Christon Tembo has dismissed media reports that Chambishi copper mine has been sold to a Chinese company.

- Opposition parties challenging President Frederick Chiluba's credentials has refused to close their electoral petition case until the court rules on an application that Chiluba and his alleged father undergo DNA tests.
- Zimbabwean high commissioner Tirivafi Kangai says visits to Zimbabwe by former president Kenneth Kaunda should not create unneccessary fears and animosity in Lusaka.
- The drug enforcement commission has arrested a Briton for trying to export cannabis.
